Predicted Survival, Hazard or Cumulative Hazard of the Fitted Models

Source: R/predict_survival.R
predict_survival.Rd

Predicts the survival probability, the hazard or the cumulative hazard of each fitted model at the given times, for each arm (the arm of an independent fit, every arm for a dependent fit), with the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the arm for comparison. Used for the landmark survival probabilities (for example every 4 weeks up to the time horizon) and for the curves of the plots.

Usage

predict_survival(
  x,
  times,
  type = c("survival", "hazard", "cumhaz"),
  conf_int = FALSE,
  n_sim = 1000,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

times

Non-negative times in the time unit of the data.

type

"survival" (the default), "hazard" or "cumhaz".

conf_int

Logical; TRUE to add simulated confidence limits. The default is FALSE.

n_sim

Number of simulated parameter vectors for the confidence limits. The default is 1000.

seed

Seed of the simulation, a single whole number. The default is 1.

Value

A data frame with the columns fit_type, arm (the arm predicted), model, time, est, lcl and ucl (NA without conf_int) and km (for type = "survival", the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the arm, and NA after its largest observed time; NA for the other types).

Details

The predictions are those of summary.flexsurvreg(). The confidence limits, when requested, are the quantiles of the predictions for n_sim parameter vectors drawn from the asymptotic normal distribution of the estimates on the transformed scale (flexsurv's normboot.flexsurvreg()); the random number generator is seeded with seed for each model and arm, so that the limits do not depend on the other models fitted, and the state of the generator of the session is restored afterwards. At time 0 the survival is set to 1, the cumulative hazard to 0 and the hazard to NA (it is infinite or undefined for some models), without calling flexsurv.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = NULL)
predict_survival(fits, times = seq(0, 60, by = 12))
